A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dyspnea is a distressing symptom for patients who are dying, and it is common for patients to seek emergency care when it occurs.

the use of opioids for palliation of symptoms in dying patients is supported by a growing body of literature, and the use of opioids in this population should not be withheld due to concerns of respiratory depression.
the management of dyspnoea in the emergency department is challenging, and the management of the patient with advanced disease and dyspnoea is even more difficult.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the management of shortness of breath in the dying patient is largely symptomatic, and that the early involvement of hospice services can facilitate optimal symptom control.
emergency physicians can play a vital role in the care of dying patients by managing symptoms and facilitating timely transitions of care to palliative and hospice services when appropriate.
